key_insight: Target-domain adaptation improved prediction of sustained antibiotic exposure in ICU patients with intracerebral hemorrhage, raising held-out AUROC from 0.782 to 0.841.
clinical_relevance: The model predicts antibiotic exposure patterns, not infection or antibiotic need, and may support research into variation in ICU care.
method: Used 2,024 MIMIC-IV ICU stays as the source cohort and 1,277 eICU stays for target-domain development and evaluation.
Combined 16 model probabilities with clinical, availability, and measurement-density features in a penalized logistic ensemble.
Evaluated sustained antibiotic exposure on at least two ICU days in 511 held-out eICU stays.
evidence_signal: Among 511 held-out stays with 48 positive outcomes, the adapted model achieved AUROC 0.841 (95% CI 0.775–0.899), average precision 0.540, and an AUROC gain of 0.059 (95% CI 0.003–0.112) over the source-only stack.
watch_item: Some inputs used the full first 24 hours, potentially including observations after antibiotics began, which limits interpretation as a pre-treatment prediction tool.
paper_title: Cross-database adaptation of machine learning models for predicting sustained antibiotic exposure among patients with intracerebral hemorrhage in intensive care units
